newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi defence minister says bomb probe continuing.
newsitem.headline: Saudi defence minister says bomb probe continuing.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's defence minister said in remarks published on Saturday a Saudi probe into a bombing that killed 19 U.S. soldiers last June was continuing but remained tight-lipped on the progress of the investigation.

"(Saudi) Interior Minister Prince Nayef made it clear in the past that it would not be appropriate to discuss the results of the investigations into this matter before they end," defence chief Prince Sultan told the London-based al-Hayat newspaper.

Prince Sultan is due to visit Paris on Saturday and continue to Washington for what diplomats described as "uneasy talks" that are expected to cover the blast at a military housing complex in the eastern city of al-Khobar in June, a potential sale of U.S. fighter jets to Riyadh and Middle East peace.
The al-Khobar bombing, in which 19 American soldiers were killed, came less than a year after a bombing in Riyadh killed five Americans and two Indians.
The Saudi defence minister said that the kingdom did not suffer from "terrorism problems".

Asked if he expected the United States to carry out a military attack on Iran if the investigation proved any Iranian involvement in al-Khobar bombing, Sultan said: "Concerning the American position, it is preferable that you pose the question to the Americans."
He said Saudi ties with Washington were "at their best."
The Washington talks are set against the backdrop of official American complaints that the Saudis are not telling Washington enough about the bombing probe.
U.S. media reports have alleged that the Saudi authorities have uncovered Iranian involvement in the blast.
Prince Sultan said Saudi Arabia was interested in good ties with Iran but urged the non-Arab regional power to stay out of the internal affairs of other countries.
"Iran is a neighbouring Moslem country and we are interested that relations should be their best," he said.

"Maybe Iran realises the fact, the importance of having positive relations between us. The presence of such a relationship requires good intentions and non-interference in internal affairs. Closeness and cooperation cannot be reached by force..."
